A prolonged October heat wave settled over the North Bay on Saturday, Oct. 3, pushing temperatures toward 100 degrees across parts of Sonoma and Napa counties as forecasters extended a heat advisory through Wednesday night.
The National Weather Service extended the advisory until 10 p.m. Wednesday for the majority of the North Bay, where afternoon temperatures could reach the mid-90s to low 100s in the coming days.
A group of East Bay friends cool off in the shade of the Healdsburg Veterans Memorial Bridge, Saturday, October 3, 2026. With the temperature near or at the century mark, families flocked to the river to escape the heat. (Kent Porter / The Press Democrat)
A group of East Bay friends cool off in the shade of the Healdsburg Veterans Memorial Bridge, Saturday, October 3, 2026. With the temperature near or at the century mark, families flocked to the river to escape the heat. (Kent Porter / The Press Democrat)
A group of kids from the East Bay cool off in the water in the shade of the Healdsburg Veterans Memorial Bridge, Saturday, October 3, 2026. With the temperature near or at the century mark, families flocked to the river to escape the heat. (Kent Porter / The Press Democrat)
1 of 3
A group of East Bay friends cool off in the shade of the Healdsburg Veterans Memorial Bridge, Saturday, October 3, 2026. With the temperature near or at the century mark, families flocked to the river to escape the heat. (Kent Porter / The Press Democrat)
Temperatures Saturday reached about 98 degrees in Santa Rosa, 96 in Sebastopol and 97 in Petaluma. Further north, Cloverdale reached about 99 degrees, while the city of Sonoma hit about 98.
In Napa County, temperatures reached about 97 degrees in Napa, 93 in American Canyon and with St. Helena soaring to 101 degrees.
The heat was accompanied by dry conditions. In Santa Rosa, relative humidity was about 18% during the hottest part of the afternoon. Across the North Bay’s interior mountains, humidity dropped as low as 15%, according to the weather service.
Higher elevations, including around Sonoma Mountain, remained relatively calm Saturday, with ridge winds around 5 mph or less during the day. Gusts were expected to reach 20 mph Saturday evening and 20 to 30 mph Sunday along exposed ridges and upper slopes.
Little relief from the heat is expected through the middle of next week, with temperatures remaining well into the 90s across many inland communities through Wednesday. A more noticeable cooldown is expected beginning Thursday, Oct. 8. with temperatures in both counties expected to settle into the 70s.
You can reach Staff Writer Isabel Beer at isabel.beer@pressdemocrat.com.

Weather Forecasts Predict Heatwave, Thunderstorms in Morocco
Morocco is set for contrasting weather conditions on Sunday, with hot temperatures forecast in the south and thunderstorms expected in several regions.
Agadir – Morocco is expected to experience hot weather in southern provinces and the Souss region on Sunday, while thunderstorms are expected in several mountainous and eastern areas, according to the General Directorate of Meteorology (DGM).
Temperatures will remain relatively high in the interior plains, with the eastern and central regions expected to become warmer.
The relatively stable and warm conditions in these areas contrast with the weather in other parts of the country, where rainfall and flooding have affected several regions in recent days.
Morning and nighttime low clouds are expected to form along the central coast, with fog likely to develop in some areas.
The DGM also forecasts dense cloud cover in the morning over the Rif, Saiss, Oulmes, and the northwestern plains. These areas could see isolated thunderstorms.
Unstable clouds will develop over the High Atlas and Middle Atlas, as well as neighboring areas, the Rif, the eastern region, and the Sahara provinces.
The forecast shows significant differences in weather conditions across the country, with some regions continuing to experience unstable weather while others record warmer and more stable conditions.
Moderate to fairly strong wind gusts are also expected over the Anti-Atlas and the Sahara provinces. The winds could cause localized dust to blow in some areas, potentially reducing visibility.
Minimum temperatures will range between 7°C and 12°C in the Atlas and Rif mountains.
The Sahara provinces and the Souss region will record the highest minimum temperatures, ranging between 24°C and 30°C.
Temperatures will range from 14°C to 20°C in the eastern region and areas near the coast. Other parts of the country will see minimum temperatures between 20°C and 24°C.
Temperatures are expected to rise in the eastern and central regions, while they will fall or remain stable in the rest of the country.
Marine conditions will remain slightly rough in the Mediterranean and along the Strait of Gibraltar. The Atlantic coast will see slightly rough to rough seas.

Imaaraadka oo warbixin ka soo saaray duuliyihii weeraray kabtanka diyaaradii u socotay Israa'iil iyo wixii u weerarka u adeegsaday
Published
Waqtiga akhriska: 5 daqiiqo
Xeer-ilaaliyaha Guud ee Imaaraadka Carabta, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, ayaa sheegay in baaritaannadu ay muujiyeen in duuliyaha labaad ee diyaaradda Flydubai uu isku dayay inuu fuliyo "fal argagixiso".
Waxa uu xusay in uu qorshihiisa bilaabay xilli ay diyaaradda hawada ku jirtay, isagoo kabtanka diyaaradda ku weeraray gudaha qolkii duuliyeyaasha, isagoo adeegsanaya faas loogu talagalay xaaladaha degdegga ah, isla markaana isku dayay inuu la wareego kontoroolka diyaaradda, sida laga soo xigtay wakaaladda Wararka Imaaraadka ee rasmiga ah WAM.
Sida uu sheegay Al Shamsi, "Baaritaannadu weli way socdaan si loo ogaado dhammaan duruufihii ku xeernaa dhacdada, ujeeddooyinkeeda iyo xiriirrada la xiriira, iyadoo sidoo kale la dhammaystirayo baaritaannada farsamo iyo hubinta caddeymaha jireed iyo kuwa dijitaalka ah. Natiijooyinka kama dambaysta ahna waxaa la shaacin doonaa sida ugu dhakhsaha badan marka la dhammaystiro habraacyada lagama maarmaanka ah."
Mas'uuliyiinta Imaaraadka Carabta ayaa xaqiijiyay inay bilaabeen baaritaanka dhacdada, iyadoo Xeer-ilaaliyaha Guud uu faray in "la xaqiijiyo heerka uu dhacdadani xiriir ula leedahay wax kasta oo ah fal ama ujeeddo argagixiso, ama in hore loo sii qorsheeyay ama loo abaabulay."
Xeer-ilaalinta guud ee Imaaraadka Carabta ma uusan shaacin dhalashada duuliyaha labaad sida lagu sheegay baaritaanno ay Sabtidii baahisay Wakaaladda Wararka ee Imaaraadka (WAM) balse il-wareed Sacuudi ah ayaa u xaqiijiyay wakaaladda wararka ee AFP inuu ahaa nin u dhashay dalka Cumaan.
Duuliyihii labaad ee weerarka qaaday wuxuu ahaa muwaadin u dhashay Cumaan, sida uu sheegay Ra'iisul Wasaaraha Israa'iil Benjamin Netanyahu.
Warbaahinno badan oo warbaahino ay ka mid yihiin Reuters, CNN iyo The New York Times ayaa magaciisa ku sheegay Hamam al-Hammami. Hase yeeshee, arrintan weli ma jirto cid rasmi ah oo xaqiijisay.
Intii uu ka shaqeynayay shirkad diyaaradeed oo kale, Oman Air, warbaahinta Maraykanka ayaa sheegtay in Al-Hammami laga saaray tababarka duuliyenimada sababo la xiriira walaac laga qabay aragtiyihiisa xagjirka ah, waxaana loo dhiibay xil kale oo ka tirsan shirkadda diyaaradaha qaranka Cumaan.
Jaamacadda Buckinghamshire New University ee UK ayaa sheegtay inuu dhammaystay koorso saddex sano ah oo waxbarasho aan toos ahayn, isla markaana uu 2023 ku qalin-jabiyay shahaado jaamacadeed oo ku saabsan maaraynta duulista. Jaamacaddu waxay intaas ku dartay inuusan halkaas ku qaadan wax tababar duuliyenimo ah.
Isagoo la hadlayay Fox News, Netanyahu wuxuu sheegay in kaddib markii weeraryahanka lagu qabtay diyaaradda, uu shaqaalaha diyaaradda ku qayliyay: "I dila, i dila!"
Ra'iisul Wasaaraha Israa'iil wuxuu intaas ku daray: "Sidaas darteed, waxaa cad inuu doonayay inuu isdilo… waxayna u muuqataa inay aad u badan tahay inuu doonayay inuu diyaaradda soo rido."
Xeer-ilaaliyaha guud ee Imaaraadka Carabta, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, ayaa sheegay in baaritaannada dhacdada ay muujinayaan in duuliyihii labaad uu isku dayay inuu fuliyo "fal argagixiso," sida ay sheegtay wakaaladda wararka rasmiga ah ee dalka.
Warbixinada qotada dheer iyo wararka BBC Somali oo toos kuugu imanaaya WhatsApp.
Halkaan kaga soo biir
Dhamaadka xayeysiinta
Duuliyihi kale ee weerarka ku dhaawacmay Machchhar, ayaa loo qaaday isbitaal, ka hor inta aan diyaarad caafimaad loogu qaadin Abu Dhabi, halkaas oo lagu soo warramay inuu ku jiro xaalad caafimaad oo deggan.
Duuliyaha, oo u dhashay Hindiya, ayaa "caafimaadkiisu wanaagsan yahay, si fiicanna u soo kabanaya," sida ay Khamiistii sheegtay safaaradda Hindiya ee Imaaraadka Carabta.
Machchhar ayaa yiri: "Waxaan ku kalsoonahay inaan soo kaban doono, mar kalena aan caafimaad qab taam ah noqdo."
Qiyaastii laba saacadood iyo bar kaddib markii diyaaradda ay ka duushay Garoonka Caalamiga ah ee Dubai, ayay si xooggan oo degdeg ah hoos uga hoobatay heerkii duulimaadkeeda.
Diyaaraddu waxay marka hore dirtay calaamadda "xaalad degdeg ah oo guud", oo ah koorka squawk 7700, ka hor inta aysan u wareegin squawk 7500, oo ah koorka tilmaamaya "faragelin sharci-darro ah" ama afduub diyaaradeed.
Mid ka mid ah rakaabka ayaa BBC-da uga warramay xilligii uu ogaaday in wax khaldan yihiin.
Almog Itali ayaa yiri: "Si kedis ah ayay diyaaraddii u billowday inay, sidii leexada oo kale, hoos ugu dhacdo iyadoo leh xoog aad u weyn oo G-force ah. Waxay si xawli ah hoos ugu dhacaysay 20 ama 30 ilbiriqsi, dabadeed way degtay, ka dibna mar kale ayay hoos u billowday."
Madaxweynaha Israa'iil Isaac Herzog ayaa Khamiistii sheegay in digniinta lagu bixiyay gudaha diyaaradda ay ahayd haweeney Israa'iili ah oo lagu magacaabo Tali Manes, taas oo maqashay sawaxan iyo buuq ka imanayay qolka duuliyeyaasha.
Ninkeeda, Zvika, oo ay weheliyaan saddex nin oo kale Yaniv Hayun, Dr Shota Musayev iyo Asaf Rajuan, ayaa galay qolka duuliyeyaasha kaddib markii Kabtan Machchhar, inkastoo uu dhaawacnaa, uu ku guuleystay inuu albaabka furo.
Hayun, ayaa muuqaal ay baahisay xafiiska ra'iisul wasaaraha ku sheegay in weeraryahanku "isku dayayay inuu burburiyo qalabka si uu diyaaradda uga dhigo mid aan la maamuli karin."
Hayun, ayaa sidoo kale sheegay inuu weeraryahanka qoorta ka qabtay, isaga oo bannaanka uga soo jiiday qolka duuliyeyaasha, ka hor inta aysan rakaab kale ka caawin inay dhulka ku dhigaan.
Wareysi uu CNN siiyay fiidnimadii Arbacada, Netanyahu wuxuu sheegay in duuliyihii la mindiyeeyay, rakaabkii iyo shaqaalihii kale ee diyaaradda ay "ku guuleysteen inay ka hortagaan musiibo la mid ah tii 9/11."

articles.full_text:
Dubai’s AC-to-heat switch: What constant temperature change does to your body, skin
- PUBLISHED: Sun 4 Oct 2026, 8:29 AM
In Dubai, summer often means living between two extremes: a sharply chilled office, mall or car, followed moments later by intense outdoor heat and humidity. While the body is designed to adapt to changing temperatures, repeatedly moving between these environments can place extra strain on its cooling systems and on the skin barrier.
“When you step into extreme heat, blood vessels near the skin widen to help release heat, the heart works harder, and the body sweats to cool itself,” said Dr Negin Hakim, Family Medicine Consultant. “In Dubai’s humidity, sweat does not evaporate as easily, so this cooling process becomes less effective.”
Back indoors, strong air-conditioning reduces the need for cooling but can bring a different set of issues. Cold, dry air may irritate the eyes, nose, throat and airways, especially in people with asthma, allergies or sinus problems. Doctors stress, however, that going from hot to cold does not directly cause a cold or flu. “These illnesses are caused by viruses, not by temperature changes themselves,” Dr Hakim said.
Stay up to date with the latest news. Follow KT on WhatsApp Channels.
The repeated switch can still leave some people feeling unwell. Headaches, fatigue, poor concentration and light-headedness are more likely when a person is dehydrated or has not eaten properly. Heat causes blood vessels to widen while sweating leads to fluid and salt loss; together, this can lower blood pressure and contribute to dizziness. Dr Hakim added that large indoor-outdoor temperature differences may contribute to dizziness, dryness of the eyes and throat, nasal congestion, runny nose and tiredness.
For the skin, the effect can be equally frustrating. Dr Maurizio Viel, Plastic Surgeon, described Dubai’s summer as two climates in one day. Outdoors, heat increases sweating and oil production. Indoors, air-conditioning strips moisture from the air, encouraging water to evaporate from the skin’s surface.
“The result is a common summer paradox: Skin that is oily and dehydrated at the same time,” he said. “Patients often respond by using harsh cleansers and acids, which damages the skin barrier further and can trigger more oil production.”
Residents may notice tightness after showering, flaking around the nose and mouth, redness, breakouts, heat rash, puffiness and makeup that no longer sits smoothly. Most of these changes are temporary and can improve within weeks with gentler skincare and better hydration.
The more lasting concern is cumulative sun and heat exposure. UV and heat can contribute to pigmentation, collagen breakdown, fine lines and loss of firmness over time. People prone to melasma or post-inflammatory pigmentation may find symptoms worsen during the hottest months, he added.
Doctors advise residents to keep indoor temperatures comfortable rather than excessively cold, avoid sitting directly under air vents, and drink water regularly throughout the day — including while indoors.
Dr Somayeh Shamsei, Specialist Internal Medicine at Aster Clinic, JLT, said the effect can be more noticeable in older adults, pregnant women, people with diabetes, and those with heart conditions. “Heat exposure can cause peripheral blood vessel dilation, an increased heart rate and a mild fall in blood pressure. Moving into a cold area reverses these changes, which can be problematic in people with pre-existing cardiac issues.”
When heading outside, take a moment to adjust, avoid rushing into strenuous activity and limit time outdoors during peak heat where possible. Hats, sunglasses, shade and broad-spectrum SPF 50 sunscreen remain essential, with reapplication every two hours when outdoors, doctors said.
For skincare, experts recommend a gentle cleanser, moisturiser containing barrier-supporting ingredients such as ceramides or niacinamide, and avoiding overuse of strong acids and retinoids during peak summer. A humidifier may also help in bedrooms or heavily air-conditioned spaces.
Residents should not dismiss persistent dizziness, unusual fatigue, wheezing, ongoing cough or shortness of breath as simple “summer fatigue”. Headache, nausea, heavy sweating, marked weakness or reduced urination after heat exposure may signal dehydration or heat exhaustion.

Translated by Due to the "red alert": Barcelona issue a statement regarding El Clásico
Barcelona issued a statement on Saturday evening over the eagerly awaited Clasico, due to take place tomorrow, Sunday, in the Spanish women's league, after a deterioration in weather conditions.
According to Mundo Deportivo, Barcelona struck an agreement to change the Clasico's kick-off time following negotiations with Real Madrid and officials of the women's Liga.
In an official statement, the club confirmed tomorrow's match will now kick off at 19:00 rather than the 17:00 slot originally set.
The Catalan club explained that all parties had agreed the new time, factoring in the weather forecast and organisational requirements.
The statement added: "The confirmation of the new time comes as far in advance as possible, to make things easier for members and supporters, and to enable them to plan their journeys and attend the match with more time and greater comfort."
Barcelona stressed: "Small, foldable umbrellas are permitted into the stadium, whereas long, rigid umbrellas are not permitted in accordance with the safety regulations in force."
Over at AS, meanwhile, the storm battering the Catalan coast is reported to keep the red alert in place until 14:00 on Sunday afternoon.
Forecasts point to a sharp rise in the probability of rainfall across Catalonia, along with an increase in the level of risk.

The demonstrations extend a crisis that has gone on for more than a week, triggered by the eviction last month of a pensioner from her Madrid flat.
MADRID: Tens of thousands of protesters marched in Madrid and other cities in Spain on Saturday to demand affordable housing, a day after lawmakers rejected relief measures for tenants.
The demonstrations extended a crisis that has gone on for more than a week, triggered by the eviction last month of a pensioner, 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal, from her Madrid flat.
The defeat was another political setback for Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and has renewed questions over whether his minority government can survive until the next scheduled general election in 2027.
His government’s proposed measures, which included automatic renewal of tenancy contracts and restrictions on evicting vulnerable tenants, were voted down by opposition parties on Friday in Spain’s parliament.
The defeat infuriated those protesting the country’s increasingly expensive housing market.
Hundreds of protesters have been occupying a tent city set up a week ago in the heart of Madrid to press for reforms.
Late on Saturday groups of far-right protesters, some of them performing Nazi salutes, tried to get to the camp but were blocked by police.
One video posted on the website of Spanish daily El Pais showed police chasing some members of the group through the streets and the newspaper also reported that officers had made three arrests.
General strike call
Earlier Saturday, demonstrators marched through the capital’s streets. Authorities said 70,000 people participated, but the organisers put the figure at 500,000.
Smaller demonstrations took place in other cities, including Palma de Mallorca, Santander, Segovia and Toledo. In Valencia, five people were arrested after clashes with police, local media reported.
At the Madrid protest Marcos Sainz, a librarian of 26, said he used to rent a two-bedroom apartment with friends for a total monthly rent of 900 euros. Today, a one-bedroom flat often costs 1,000 euros — or half the median monthly salary in the capital, he told AFP.
He would protest rental spikes “until someone dares to regulate it all as (otherwise) we’ll all have to leave Madrid and that would be a shame as I am from Madrid”.
“We are demanding a fundamental right,” said Javier, a 31-year-old solar panel installer. “Decent housing, stability and conditions allowing us to construct a decent life project.
“I spend half of my salary on a tiny room,” he added.
Valeria Racu, one of the spokesmen of the Tenants’ Union organising the protest, said in a statement that the last eight days’ protests had shown the effectiveness of people’s power.
“Now begins real politics — politics which has always belonged to the people and which will return once and for all to the streets,” she added.
She repeated her union’s call for a general strike.
Calls for early election
Housing has for years been a top concern for Spaniards as supply falls short of demand, with rents and house prices rising as elsewhere in the EU.
Average rents in Spain have almost doubled over the past decade, while asking prices for homes have risen by about 90%, according to real estate website Idealista.
Abascal’s eviction catalysed long-running anger about runaway housing costs.
The pensioner was forced to leave the Madrid flat where she had lived for more than seven decades after it was acquired by an investment company that sought to increase her rent by 275%, say housing campaigners.
The backlash led the property’s new owners to reach a deal allowing her to return to the flat at a low rent.
The housing bills Sanchez’s leftist coalition had presented to parliament were rejected after the Catalan separatist party Junts — on whose support the government relies — voted against them, arguing they lacked rigour.
Junts joined the main opposition Popular Party (PP) and the far-right Vox party in shooting down the measures.
PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo on Saturday urged Sanchez to call early elections “because the country can’t take any more”.
Recent opinion polls have generally placed the Popular Party ahead of the Socialists.

articles.full_text:
Dry soil and a heat wave make each other worse. Ground with no moisture left stops cooling the air above it, and hotter air pulls still more out of the soil. Across the lower 48 states, those two conditions now show up in the same summer week often enough that researchers have started mapping them as a single hazard.
The map runs county by county across 22 summers, and those days are not distributed evenly. Counties with the most of them tend to have more than one disadvantage already. That can mean low household income, houses built before 1950, or many residents with no health insurance.
It counts exposure, not damage. Weekly drought grades come from the national Drought Monitor, and daily high temperatures from NOAA’s Climate Prediction Center. A day counts when the county was in drought and unusually hot for the season.
“What surprised us most was how much the picture changed when we looked at vulnerabilities together rather than one at a time,” Mishra told Earth.com.
Outdoor workers face more exposure
The team sorted counties by the work most people there do. Farming, mining, and outdoor recreation went in one group, manufacturing and government work in the other.
Under milder drought conditions, outdoor-work counties averaged roughly six to eight combined heat-and-drought days each summer, compared with about four to five in indoor-work counties. As drought became more severe, the number of combined days fell in both groups, but outdoor-work counties still had more.
A couple of days a summer is a small gap on a chart. It is bigger if those days are spent in a field.
“This matters because a farm worker, for example, may spend much of the day outdoors during periods when drought and extreme heat occur, while an office worker may have greater protection in an air-conditioned indoor environment,” Mishra said.
Farm counties logged the longest spells
Severe combined days concentrated in the South, the Southeast, and the West. Median severe days rose as poverty rates rose, though loosely enough that chance can’t be ruled out. Farm employment tracked it more closely.
Among high-poverty counties, Jim Hogg County, Texas, topped the list at about 11.5 severe days a summer, with Apache County, Arizona, near 9.5. Among counties where more than 10% of the workforce farms, King County, Texas, came in around 10.2 days, and Stanton County, Kansas, around 8 to 8.5.
State by state, 34% of Georgia’s counties landed in both the high-poverty and high-exposure groups, and 33% of Texas counties were farm-heavy and heavily exposed. In those corridors a bad summer costs a paycheck as well as a water bill, and crop losses land on the same places.
Older housing adds to vulnerability
Houses built before 1950 are the study’s stand-in for homes that heat up and stay hot. On its own, nationally, that measure didn’t line up with more severe days at all.
Pair it with something else and the picture changes. Asked by Earth.com what the pairings did, Mishra came back to housing.
“Older housing is a good example. By itself, older housing did not show a strong positive relationship with severe compound drought and heat-wave occurrence across the whole United States,” he said.
“But once older housing overlapped with poverty, lack of insurance, limited food access, medical dependency, or an elderly population, some of the strongest concentrations in the entire study appeared.”
The team measured that with a Gini coefficient, a number from 0 to 1 for how unevenly something is shared out. In counties with both high poverty rates and older housing, the most exposed 20% of residents accounted for nearly 80% of the combined days. Adding low educational attainment pushed the concentration higher still.
Regional risks vary across the U.S.
Which disadvantage lines up with exposure changes by region. Southwestern counties showed the strongest link with lack of health insurance, which accounted for about 69% of the local relationship between social conditions and severe combined days.
Across the West, dependence on electrically powered medical equipment – the kind counted in the federal emPOWER program – accounted for 63%, while older adults accounted for 16%. In the Southeast, older housing and low educational attainment accounted for 21% to 25%, and poverty for 12%.
Some western and Great Basin counties recorded long severe spells despite low poverty rates. Parts of Appalachia had the opposite.
“So the social vulnerability map and the climate-hazard map do not simply mirror one another. The critical locations are where those two geographies intersect,” Mishra said.
Exposure does not equal harm
The maps count days when drought and extreme heat were present in the same county, and nothing more. No heat deaths, no hospital visits, no dollar figure for a ruined field.
The links are associations, not causes, and the model kept only the positive ones, so it marks where disadvantage and exposure overlap rather than what drives risk. Housing age is a rough stand-in, and Mishra’s team said it can’t fully capture housing quality or access to cooling.
County averages hide what happens inside a county. A single rural county can be larger than some states, and the same uneven pattern turns up inside cities at the neighborhood level. Where county data were missing, the team filled gaps from neighbors, smoothing local spikes.
Climate data ends in 2021
The last summer in the dataset is 2021, and the weather since hasn’t settled down. The historic drought of 2026 covered more than 60% of the country by May.
Mishra expects the social half of the map to hold up, because poverty, older housing, educational disadvantage, medical dependency, and limited health insurance tend to persist for years.
The social conditions may change slowly, but the climate patterns can shift much faster. Earth.com asked what it would take to determine whether those patterns have changed.
“Confirming those changes would require an updated analysis using more recent climate and socioeconomic data,” Mishra said.
Until researchers update the analysis, the newest overlap on record is five summers old.
